title: The inversion number of a path-reversed tournament: Resolving a conjecture of Belkhechine, Bouaziz, Boudabbous, and Pouzet
summary: Let $D$ be a tournament and let $X\subseteq V(D)$. The inversion of $X$ reverses all arcs whose both endpoints lie in $X$ and leaves every other arc unchanged. A family of inversions is a decycling family if applying all of them produces an acyclic, equivalently transitive, tournament. The inversion number $\inv(D)$ is the minimum size of such a family. Let $Q_n$ be the tournament on $[n]$ obtained from the natural transitive tournament by reversing precisely the consecutive pairs $12,23,\ldots,(n-1)n$.
